issues.description: Predicate is expressed as a negated conjunction with typeof, obscuring the layer-statement-vs-block invariant.
issues.detail: The condition `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` buries a double negative inside a five-clause `&&` chain. Extracting a named predicate like `isLayerStatement(node)` and phrasing the rule positively would make the CSS-spec invariant (statement-form `@layer foo;` allowed before `@import`, block-form not) self-evident to readers.

issues.description: `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` is a brittle proxy for 'statement-form at-rule'.
issues.detail: PostCSS models block presence via `nodes` being an array; statement form means `nodes` is absent. Checking `node.nodes === undefined` directly (or `Array.isArray(node.nodes)`) names the AST fact instead of probing for undefined via `typeof`, which is idiomatic only for possibly-undeclared identifiers and couples correctness to an implementation detail.

issues.description: Test coverage misses the symmetric accept-case for statement-form `@layer foo;` before `@import`.
issues.detail: The diff adds the reject case `@layer foo {}` before `@import` but does not assert that statement-form `@layer foo;` before `@import` remains accepted. Adding the complementary positive test pins down the distinction the predicate now encodes in both directions and guards against a future regression that flips the condition.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously finds the fix correct and minimal: block-bearing `@layer` is no longer mistreated as a permitted pre-`@import` construct, matching the CSS Cascade spec distinction between statement-form and block-form `@layer`. All three reviewers converge on the same three polish items — the predicate reads as a double negative, `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` is a brittle proxy for AST shape, and the test suite covers only one side of the new distinction. Nothing rises above P2; safe to merge with a clearer predicate and a symmetric statement-form test.
